newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Nov forex reserves fall to $525.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Nov forex reserves fall to $525.1 mln.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank said on Wednesday its foreign exchange reserves fell to $525.1 million by November 30 from $541 million at the end of October.
The BNB said interventions to support the ailing lev helped whittle down reserves. The lev hit a record low 413 to the dollar on Thursday.

Last month, the central bank said it would aim to preserve reserves for the possible introduction of a currency board system, which would mean money in circulation must be matched by the hard currency reserves.

The BNB said some $500 million reserves plus the strategic gold reserves worth $450 million were enough to comply with a currency board system at the start but were insufficient to cover pending foreign debt payments of around $300 million due in the first quarter of next year.
The International Monetary Fund said it would support the implementation of the currency board system with substantial loans within Bulgaria's $580 million quota in the fund.

The government said the currency board system is expected to be implemented at the beginning of next year, after parliament approves a 1997 budget and banking laws amendments to make the system operational. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
